tasks.request: Implement share-token access and revocation in src/service.py, preserving the ordinary owner lookup. read_shared(connection, token, now) returns only {'id': document_id, 'title': title} when the exact token exists, is not revoked, expires_at is strictly greater than now, and its document is active and belongs to the tenant recorded on the token. Otherwise return None, with no writes. revoke_share(connection, tenant, owner, token) returns True and commits revocation only when both the token and its active document belong to that tenant and the document belongs to that owner. Authorized repeated revocation returns True; unknown, wrong-tenant, wrong-owner or deleted-document tokens return False with no changes. Expiration does not prevent an authorized revocation. now and expires_at are integer epoch seconds supplied by callers, with no wall-clock dependency. Bind SQL parameters, including tokens with quotes. Start in src/service.py and src/repository.py.

sys.path.insert(0, os.getcwd())
import sqlite3
from src.repository import initialize
from src.service import read_owned, read_shared, revoke_share
c = sqlite3.connect(":memory:")
initialize(c)
c.executemany("INSERT INTO documents VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?)", [(1,"a","owner","A",0), (2,"b","owner","B",0), (3,"a","owner","Deleted",1), (4,"a","other","Other",0)])
c.executemany("INSERT INTO shares VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?)", [("good",1,"a",200,0), ("expired",1,"a",100,0), ("revoked",1,"a",200,1), ("cross",2,"a",200,0), ("deleted",3,"a",200,0), ("other",4,"a",200,0), ("orphan",99,"a",200,0), ("q' OR 1=1 --",1,"a",200,0)])
c.commit()
assert read_shared(c, "good", 199) == {"id":1,"title":"A"}
for token in ("good", "expired"):
    assert read_shared(c, token, 200) is None
assert read_shared(c, "expired", 100) is None
for token in ("revoked", "cross", "deleted", "orphan", "missing", "' OR 1=1 --"):
    assert read_shared(c, token, 50) is None
assert read_shared(c, "q' OR 1=1 --", 50) == {"id":1,"title":"A"}
before = c.execute("SELECT * FROM shares ORDER BY token").fetchall()
for tenant, owner, token in [("b","owner","good"), ("a","wrong","good"), ("a","owner","cross"), ("a","owner","deleted"), ("a","owner","other"), ("a","owner","missing"), ("a' OR 1=1 --","owner","good")]:
    assert revoke_share(c, tenant, owner, token) is False
    assert c.execute("SELECT * FROM shares ORDER BY token").fetchall() == before
assert revoke_share(c, "a", "owner", "good") is True
assert revoke_share(c, "a", "owner", "good") is True
assert read_shared(c, "good", 50) is None
assert revoke_share(c, "a", "owner", "expired") is True
assert revoke_share(c, "a", "owner", "q' OR 1=1 --") is True
assert read_owned(c, "a", "owner", 1) == {"id":1,"title":"A"}
assert read_shared(c, "other", 50) == {"id":4,"title":"Other"}
assert not c.in_transaction

tasks.request: Fix iter_lines(source) in src/reader.py and src/service.py.collect_lines. source is an iterable yielding byte chunks with close(). Decode UTF-8 strictly across arbitrary chunk boundaries, including multibyte characters. Split on LF; remove one immediately preceding CR, preserve other characters and empty lines, and emit a nonempty final unterminated line. A trailing newline creates no additional line. Empty byte chunks have no effect and an empty source returns no lines. Be lazy: once a complete line is available, yield it before requesting another source chunk. No whole-source buffering. Close a started source exactly once on exhaustion, explicit iterator close(), source errors or decoding errors; an unstarted iterator has no source effects. collect_lines delegates to iter_lines and returns a list. Source.close does not raise. Start in src/reader.py and src/service.py.

import os, sys
sys.path.insert(0, os.getcwd())
from src.chunks import Chunks
from src.reader import iter_lines
from src.service import collect_lines
encoded = "á\nβ\r\n\nlast\r".encode("utf-8")
chunks = [encoded[index:index+1] for index in range(len(encoded))]
source = Chunks(chunks)
assert collect_lines(source) == ["á", "β", "", "last\r"]
assert source.closes == 1
for chunks, expected in [([], []), ([b"", b""], []), ([b"\n"], [""]), ([b"a\n\n"], ["a", ""]), ([b"a\r", b"\n", b"b"], ["a", "b"]), ([b"a\rb\n"], ["a\rb"]), ([b"head", b"", b"tail"], ["headtail"])]:
    source = Chunks(chunks)
    assert collect_lines(source) == expected
    assert source.closes == 1
source = Chunks([b"one\ntwo\n", b"three\n"])
stream = iter_lines(source)
assert (source.reads, source.closes) == (0, 0)
assert next(stream) == "one"
assert next(stream) == "two"
assert (source.reads, source.closes) == (1, 0)
stream.close()
stream.close()
assert (source.reads, source.closes) == (1, 1)
source = Chunks([b"unused"])
iter_lines(source).close()
assert (source.reads, source.closes) == (0, 0)
for chunks in ([b"\xff"], [b"\xc3"], [b"ok\n", b"\xe2", b"bad"]):
    source = Chunks(chunks)
    try:
        collect_lines(source)
    except UnicodeDecodeError:
        pass
    else:
        raise AssertionError("malformed UTF-8 accepted")
    assert source.closes == 1
failure = RuntimeError("read failed")
class FailingChunks(Chunks):
    def __next__(self):
        if self.reads == 1:
            raise failure
        return super().__next__()
source = FailingChunks([b"first\n"])
stream = iter_lines(source)
assert next(stream) == "first"
try:
    next(stream)
except RuntimeError as exc:
    assert exc is failure
else:
    raise AssertionError("source error swallowed")
assert source.closes == 1

Lines contain sku and quantity. Quantity must be a positive safe integer and the batch

stock throws Error('stock unavailable'). No stock or reservation record may change on

in any line order returns the existing record without another deduction. A changed
aggregate for the same tenant/key throws Error('key conflict'). Existing-record checks
happen after input validation but before availability checks. Keep input arrays unchanged.

tenant/key share one loader invocation, while unrelated keys and tenants remain independent.
